text: linuxity guest testing: never pipe a guest run straight into a tool call (a stuck child keeps the pipe open and hangs the turn). Run detached, send output to a file, and SIGKILL after a deadline; /tmp/hvx/reg.sh is the hang-proof regression set (29 cases). For hangs, `sample <pid>` on every build-mac/linuxity process; for host crashes, read ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/linuxity-*.ips.

linuxity host-side trap cost lives in FileNamespace path handling, not the hypervisor: a single readlink distinguishes symlink/present/absent (EINVAL) and replaces lstat+lstat+readlink in classify_impl; opendir's success replaces is_dir probes in merge_dir. Profile with `sample <pid>` during `ls -lR /usr` x10 — on-CPU time should be host syscalls (lstat/readlink/getdirentries64), and any malloc/freelist frames in the sample mean a hot path is allocating per entry or per lookup.

linuxity's trap-backend contract lives in include/linuxity/runtime/backend.hpp: core SyscallTrap (start/next/resume/forward/redirect/exited/exit_code) plus named optional capabilities (RedirectsTwoPaths, ForwardsSynchronously, TranslatesSockets, ExecsThroughInterp, DeliversSignals, ReportsProcEvents). Backends live in runtime/{linux,darwin,windows}/ with host-agnostic code in runtime/shared/; tools/check_layout.sh runs as the runtime_layout ctest and forbids cross-backend includes. Never gate a backend call on a bare `if constexpr (requires {...})` — that silently forwarded untranslated guest paths; use the named capability concept so a typo fails the build. windows/ is core-only today.

linuxity has ONE main() (src/main.cpp: flags/usage/verbs for every host); per-host code is only host_run/host_internal/host_name in src/run_{linux,darwin,windows}.cpp behind src/host_run.hpp, and the guest login env is src/guest_env.hpp. macOS guest testing: Alpine aarch64 minirootfs at /tmp/alpine-a64, run via a detached runner with a SIGKILL deadline; tests build with -UNDEBUG so asserts are live.

linuxity macOS: every guest process is its own linuxity holding a Hypervisor.framework VM (hard limit 128 at once; PidSpace budgets warm zygotes, a fork with no VM is EAGAIN). Per-process state crossing a fork goes through Kernel::export_fork/import_fork (kernel/fork_state.hpp); credentials have one authority, the dispatcher's kernel::Creds via abi/creds.hpp, republished to the in-guest table by HvfTrap::ig_after_dispatch.

linuxity-tests live at /tmp/up-t/tmp/lxt (guest /tmp/lxt); run: build-mac/linuxity --root /tmp/alpine-a64 --persist /tmp/up-t /usr/bin/python3 /tmp/lxt/run.py [-v] [-j4] [area|case] via /tmp/lxrun.sh. On macOS, per-task /proc facts come from runtime/darwin/procinfo.hpp via ProcessTable::host_fact; per-task sched state (nice/policy/affinity) lives in PidSpace's shared table. musl's sched_getscheduler and Python 3.12's missing os.timerfd_create are guest-userland ENOSYS, not linuxity bugs.

The linuxity tree is often edited concurrently by another agent session (uncommitted darwin/ changes, commits landing on master mid-task). Build in a private dir (build-ux), and commit only your own hunks: git apply --cached a filtered patch of your hunks, then verify the index alone with git checkout-index into a temp dir and build/test there before committing.

tools/linux-build-check.sh compile-checks the Linux host build (GCC + musl, aarch64) from a Mac inside a linuxity Alpine env (needs LINUXITY=path-to-mac-binary; run detached with a deadline). CI only builds Linux on x86-64/glibc, so musl/aarch64 breaks (e.g. musl's #define prlimit64 prlimit) only show up there. The Linux binary can't yet RUN inside an HVF guest (no guest ptrace).

linuxity macOS HVF: vCPU handles start at 0 (never use 0 as an empty sentinel); a kick can cancel hv_vcpu_run mid EL1 detour on the vectors page (pc 0x400 in-guest svc handler, 0x800 TLB-flush stub) so HvfCpu::run unwinds to ELR/SPSR; macOS never raises SIGXCPU for vCPU-spinning threads, so RLIMIT_CPU is emulated in darwin/timer.hpp.

linuxity: the user runs ./build-ux/linuxity interactively. Never pkill/kill by a pattern that matches build-ux (or build-mac); agent tests use a private signed copy at /tmp/lx-agent/linuxity (built from build-agent) and only ever kill processes matching /tmp/lx-agent/.

macOS host bug: poll() and kqueue never report a FIFO's last writer closing, but select() does; linuxity's darwin signal_aware_poll switches to select() when a FIFO is polled for input and reports POLLHUP, and epoll_wait_guest waits on the kqueue fd + those FIFOs via signal_aware_poll. epoll_wait must never return 0 events before its timeout (libuv asserts; the linux-build-check cmake run catches it).

linuxity: agent fixes are tested on /tmp/lx-agent builds, so ./build-ux/linuxity stays stale until rebuilt (cmake --build build-ux --target linuxity; safe while the user's session is open). Before giving the user a command, rebuild build-ux and run that exact command.

linuxity filesystem torture test: tests/fs_torture.py (50 checks) — run `./build-ux/linuxity run ubuntu [--user root] --bind "$PWD/tests:/mnt/t" -- python3 /mnt/t/fs_torture.py`; expect 48/0/2 as user, 49/0/1 as root. Darwin gotchas it pinned: closing any fd drops POSIX locks (fork must not close fds in the parent), host dirs must keep owner rwx (guest search rules come from the shadow store), CPython os.link uses link() not linkat(FOLLOW).

linuxity oracle: tests/oracle.py runs 9 *_torture.py suites (process, filesystem, memory, ipc, sync, net, tty, sys, tools) as root and as uid 1000. Run `./build-ux/linuxity run ubuntu --user root --bind "$PWD/tests:/mnt/t" -- python3 /mnt/t/oracle.py`. Ground truth: real Linux via colima + tests/oracle.Dockerfile (DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/dockercfg DOCKER_HOST=unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock) passes 403/403; any check that fails there is a test bug.

XNU quirks behind two linuxity fixes: a session leader's exit blocks with no timeout until its controlling tty's output drains (proc_exit->ttywait), so end_process marks the exit final in PidSpace (exit_final) and wait4 reaps it from the table; and EVFILT_PROC on a zombie fails with ESRCH, so make_pidfd falls back to a triggered EVFILT_USER when waitid(WNOWAIT) shows the zombie.
